extracted.intended_audience: telecommunications/IP executives, analysts, and patent/IP strategy professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and metrics for understanding 5G Standard Essential Patent (SEP) declarations: taxonomy of Technical Specifications, who declares SEPs, regional and release-driven trends, which TSs are targeted, and likely future SEP focus areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Specification (TS) classification: Foundation vs Transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: ABI Research classifies 3GPP Technical Specifications into two distinct categories: Foundation Specifications and Transformation Specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundation Specifications: Address bottom layer telco protocols (signaling, modulation, control, user plane, data plane, switching, scheduling, channel coding, multiplexing, signal measurements, testing, policies, network security). Transformation Specifications: Introduce use cases, business models, paradigms like service management/orchestration, network slicing, APIs/network exposure, codec and use-case specific requirements. Note: ABI Research finds ~99% of 5G SEP declarations are Foundation Specifications produced by 3GPP WGs.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3GPP Working Group (WG) focus and influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate SEP activity by which 3GPP WGs are producing the TSs to which patents are declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RAN (Radio Access Network) focus dominates 5G declarations (97% for Rel-15, 93% for Rel-16, 86% for Rel-17). RAN1 and RAN2 are the most influential WGs, receiving 93% of the total 5G SEP contribution share. At Rel-18 outset, System Architecture (SA) WGs accounted for 72% of declarations to TSs, with Core Network and Terminals (CT) WGs contributing 28%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarant company type
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify SEP declarants by company category (infrastructure vendors, handset/UE vendors, chipset vendors, government-funded research organizations, R&D companies, network service providers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of 2022: infrastructure vendors = 21,373 declared patent families (largest share); handset/UE vendors = 18,772 families. Chipset vendors, government-funded research orgs, and R&D companies follow. Network service providers contribute heavily to 3GPP work but are far less involved with ETSI SEP declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release-timed declaration trends (Rel-15/16/17/18/19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze SEP declarations relative to 3GPP release timeline to see which company types and topics were active in each release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant traction 2017–2019 ahead of 5G launch. Infrastructure, chipset vendors, government-funded orgs were more active in Rel-15; handset vendors, R&D companies, and network service providers increased activity from 2020 (Rel-16). Infrastructure vendors (e.g., Huawei) increased involvement again in 2022. Rel-18/19 expected to shift focus to service requirements, MIMO evolution, AI/ML, energy savings, sidelink, RedCap, precise positioning, SatCom, ambient IoT, sensing/communication integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic origin of SEPs and regional distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Count declared SEP families by country/region and track regional trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Between 2017–2022 counts reported: China 24,000; South Korea 9,700; United States 6,600; Europe 5,000. Asia-Pacific dominates 5G SEPs. European SEP declarations have trended downward for the last two years. Use these counts to assess regional concentration of declared families.

rubrics_metrics.name: TSs per patent family (TS-per-family metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how many Technical Specifications are declared per patent family as a proxy for breadth of applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: European companies average 1.5 TSs per patent family versus global average 3.3 TSs per family — an indicator of how broadly patents are declared across specs in different regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations count vs unique patent families (declaration-to-family metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate raw declaration counts from unique patent families to avoid double-counting and to assess actual family-level SEP volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of 2022 ABI Research/ETSI data: roughly 172,000 5G declarations covering 51,000 unique patent families. Analysts should use both numbers: declarations show outreach/targeting; families show distinct IP assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most-targeted Technical Specifications (popularity by declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which specific TS documents receive the most SEP declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: TS 38.331 (NR RRC protocol) — 32,161 SEP declarations; TS 38.213/TS 38.214 (NR physical layer procedures for control/data) — 27,012 and 19,661 declarations respectively. Tracking which TSs are most targeted shows where companies see essential innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent office coverage and family protection breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess where SEP families are filed/protected (WIPO, USPTO, CNIPA, European offices) to understand geographic protection strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most declared SEP families have protection in multiple countries via WIPO-supported applications. WIPO families hold significant share, followed by USPTO, CNIPA, and European patent offices collectively. Use office footprint to infer licensing market focus and enforcement options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geopolitical and commercial influences on SEP strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider non-technical factors (trade restrictions, bans) that affect patenting, declaration, and licensing strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative example: the Huawei ban influenced companies to emphasize licensing revenue and WIPO applications. Geopolitical factors can reshape where firms file, how aggressively they license, and which markets they prioritize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future technology focus areas for SEP activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate technological domains likely to generate SEPs in upcoming releases and R&D cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ABI Research anticipates Rel-18/Rel-19/6G trends including NR-MIMO evolution, mobility enhancements, AI/ML across end-to-end systems, network energy savings, sidelink, XR enhancements, Reduced Capability (RedCap), precise positioning/time resilience, ambient IoT, SatCom integration, railway communications, sensing+communication, Terahertz communication, extreme energy performance, cognitive networks. Use these domains to prioritize patent monitoring and strategic filing.
